clue.text: Lamb following a maiden in Fielding novel

indicators.note: one thing following another puts the essayist's pen name after the earlier pieces

parts.note: taken as written
M is the cricket abbreviation for a maiden over
Elia was the pen name Charles Lamb used for his essays

explanation.surface: A literary critic places some lamb next to a young woman in an eighteenth-century novel.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Lamb' is not the animal: it is the essayist Charles Lamb, whose pen name was Elia. Henry Fielding's last novel is Amelia (1751).
explanation.definitionFit: Amelia is the title of a novel written by Henry Fielding, so it is an example of his books.

clue.text: Show after sort of blue film

indicators.note: after places one piece behind another, so the word for show comes second

parts.note: midnight blue is a very dark shade of blue
to express is to show a feeling

explanation.surface: A smutty screening put on after a blue movie.
explanation.walkthrough: 'blue film' suggests pornography, but 'blue' belongs with 'sort of' and 'film' alone is the definition. Midnight Express is a 1978 prison drama.
explanation.definitionFit: Midnight Express is a 1978 Alan Parker movie about an American jailed in Turkey.

clue.text: Quiet and soft, closely related clipped European dialect

indicators.note: something clipped has had its end trimmed off, so the last letter goes

parts.note: a low voice is both quiet and soft
germane means relevant or closely connected

explanation.surface: A soft-spoken, clipped European accent heard among close relatives.
explanation.definitionFit: Low German is the group of dialects spoken in the lowlands of northern Germany, as opposed to High German.

clue.text: A stiff examination

parts.note: surface reading: a tough, demanding test
setter's reading: a stiff is slang for a corpse, so this is an examination of a dead body

explanation.walkthrough: 'stiff' looks like an adjective meaning difficult, but it is the noun: slang for a dead body.
explanation.definitionFit: A post-mortem medical inspection of a corpse to find the cause of death is the procedure meant.

clue.text: Power running around central part of Tube (underground)

definitions.note: the clue's own bracket marks the definition

indicators.note: something running around another thing encircles it, so the power word goes outside

parts.note: sway is power or influence over others

indicators.note: the central part of a word means only its middle letters are kept

parts.note: the two middle letters of the word

explanation.surface: A power cable runs round the middle of a London Underground line.
explanation.walkthrough: The Tube is London's underground railway, which makes the surface look like it is defining itself; the bracketed word is the actual definition.
explanation.definitionFit: A subway is an underground railway in American usage, or an underground pedestrian passage in Britain.

clue.text: Race official in agitated state on a road

indicators.note: on in a down clue means coming next below, so the later pieces follow

parts.note: to be in a stew is to be agitated
taken as written
standard abbreviation

explanation.surface: A marshal at a road race gets flustered out on the course.
explanation.definitionFit: A steward is an official who supervises a race meeting or sporting event.

clue.text: See nobleman in pub just after

parts.note: a bar is a pub
on can mean immediately after, as in 'on arrival'

explanation.surface: An instruction to spot an aristocrat drinking in a pub shortly afterwards.
explanation.walkthrough: 'See' just introduces the clue: look for a nobleman found in the following pieces.
explanation.definitionFit: A baron is a member of the lowest rank of the peerage, a title of nobility.

clue.text: Miss a chart prepared by girl for book

indicators.note: something prepared has been made ready or reworked, so these letters are rearranged

parts.note: taken as written
Carol is a girl's name

explanation.surface: A young woman drew up a chart for a book.
explanation.definitionFit: A Christmas Carol is the 1843 novella by Charles Dickens featuring Scrooge.

clue.text: Plain-speaking skydiver is this once jump's over

definitions.meaning: first meaning: practical and unpretentious in manner

definitions.text: skydiver is this once jump's over
definitions.meaning: second meaning, taken literally: where a parachutist ends up after landing

explanation.walkthrough: The second half is a cryptic description that reads the idiom literally: a skydiver who has landed is physically back on the ground.
explanation.definitionFit: The idiom describes a sensible, practical person who speaks frankly, and literally it describes someone standing back on the ground.

clue.text: Daring bishop, advanced in years

parts.note: B is the chess abbreviation for bishop
old means advanced in years

explanation.surface: An elderly bishop who is surprisingly adventurous.
explanation.definitionFit: Bold describes someone willing to take risks, a close synonym of daring.

clue.text: Doubtful whether Fay is heartless

indicators.note: without a heart means the centre letter of the name is removed

parts.note: if can mean whether
taken as written

explanation.surface: Someone wonders whether a woman called Fay is cold and unfeeling.
explanation.definitionFit: Iffy is informal for uncertain or of questionable quality, matching doubtful.

clue.text: Suppose wood is by source of Ouse

indicators.note: the source of a river is where it begins, so only the first letter is taken

parts.note: first letter of the river's name
pine is a kind of timber

explanation.surface: Someone guesses that a wood stands near where the River Ouse begins.
explanation.walkthrough: The Ouse is the name of several English rivers.
explanation.definitionFit: To opine is to state an opinion, which is close to supposing or believing something.

clue.text: Litigant's apparent argument

parts.note: plain means clear or obvious
a tiff is a petty quarrel

explanation.surface: A party to a lawsuit makes what seems an obvious argument.
explanation.walkthrough: The 's stands for 'is', joining the definition to the wordplay.
explanation.definitionFit: A plaintiff is the person who brings a case in court, one kind of litigant.

clue.text: 24 hours travelling round in old African country

indicators.note: travelling round something circles it, so the day word wraps around the other piece

parts.note: a day lasts twenty-four hours
to be in is to be at home

explanation.surface: A day spent journeying around a former African state.
explanation.walkthrough: 'in' looks like a preposition but supplies a word itself: someone who is in is at home.
explanation.definitionFit: Dahomey was the name of the West African country now called Benin, renamed in 1975.

clue.text: Girl in hydro worried about occupational therapy

indicators.note: about means surrounding, so the shuffled letters go round the therapy abbreviation
worried suggests something agitated and disturbed, so its letters are thrown about

parts.note: taken as written; a hydro is a spa hotel
standard abbreviation

explanation.surface: A girl at a health spa is anxious about her occupational therapy session.
explanation.walkthrough: A hydro is a British spa hotel offering water treatments.
explanation.definitionFit: Dorothy is a girl's name, and crosswords often define a first name simply as girl.

clue.text: Runs round county town and ancient port

parts.note: R is the cricket abbreviation for runs
O is round in shape
Chester is the county town of Cheshire

explanation.surface: A jogger does laps around a county's principal town.
explanation.walkthrough: 'round' looks like it puts one piece inside another, but it simply gives a letter of round shape. A county town is the administrative centre of an English county.
explanation.definitionFit: Rochester in Kent is a historic port city on the River Medway, dating back to Roman times.

clue.text: Fine involving Tyneside daily

indicators.note: involving means taking something inside, so the first word holds the second

parts.note: fine weather is clear
Tyneside is in the north-east of England

explanation.surface: A penalty imposed on a newspaper from the north of England.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Fine' and 'daily' suggest a penalty and a newspaper; in Britain a daily is also a cleaning lady who comes in each day.
explanation.definitionFit: A daily is a British term for a domestic help who cleans a house on a daily or regular basis.

clue.text: Talk about role

parts.note: c. (circa) means about
wearing a different hat means taking a different role

explanation.surface: A discussion about the part someone plays.
explanation.walkthrough: 'about' looks like a link meaning 'concerning', but it supplies the circa abbreviation.
explanation.definitionFit: To chat is to talk informally, so the two are direct synonyms.

clue.text: Ill-will following Royal Engineers' temporary delay

indicators.note: following places one piece behind another, so the ill-will word comes second

parts.note: RE is the abbreviation for the Royal Engineers, a British Army corps
spite is malice or ill-will

explanation.surface: Army engineers' bad feeling causes a hold-up.
explanation.definitionFit: A respite is a short break or postponement, such as a stay of execution.

clue.text: European river fish and last of wild duck

parts.note: the Po is Italy's longest river
the char is a fish of the trout family

indicators.note: the last of a word is its final letter, so only that one is kept

parts.note: final letter of the word

explanation.surface: A list of wildlife spotted on a European river: a fish and a wild duck.
explanation.walkthrough: 'wild duck' reads as one phrase, but only 'duck' is the definition.
explanation.definitionFit: The pochard is a European diving duck, the male having a chestnut head.

clue.text: Old man playing organ is a model of perfection

parts.note: pa is an informal word for father

indicators.note: playing suggests something being performed or messed about with, so the instrument's letters are rearranged

parts.note: taken as written

explanation.surface: An elderly organist performs flawlessly.
explanation.definitionFit: A paragon is a person or thing regarded as an ideal example of excellence.

clue.text: Medicinal herb daughter not feeling well needed

parts.note: standard abbreviation
ill means unwell

explanation.surface: A sick daughter needed a herbal remedy.
explanation.definitionFit: Dill is an aromatic herb traditionally used as a remedy, as in dill water for colic.

clue.text: Antipasto — favourite is served in stewed pear

indicators.note: food served in a dish sits inside it, so these pieces go within the other letters
fruit that is stewed is cooked down and broken up, so its letters are rearranged

parts.note: taken as written
taken as written
a teacher's pet is a favourite

explanation.surface: A menu note: the favourite starter comes in a stewed pear.
explanation.definitionFit: Antipasto is the Italian first course, a small dish eaten before the main meal to stimulate the appetite.

clue.text: Greek character volunteers after article

indicators.note: after places one piece behind another, so the volunteers come second

parts.note: the definite article
the TA was the Territorial Army, Britain's volunteer reserve force

explanation.surface: A Greek person signs up after reading a newspaper article.
explanation.definitionFit: Theta is the eighth letter of the Greek alphabet, and a character here means a letter.

clue.text: Perform extremely well with former church leader in local

parts.note: ex- means former
CE is the Church of England

indicators.note: the leader of a word is its front letter, so just that one is taken

parts.note: first letter of the word

explanation.surface: Someone shines while drinking with an ex-vicar in their neighbourhood pub.
explanation.walkthrough: 'church leader' looks like a bishop or minister, but the phrase splits: 'church' gives CE and 'leader in local' gives one letter. A local is a British word for one's nearby pub.
explanation.definitionFit: To excel is to be outstandingly good at something, surpassing ordinary performance.

clue.text: Venus, usually, has smoothing and subtle arts

parts.note: evening out a surface smooths it

indicators.note: something subtle is crafty and devious, hinting the letters are cunningly rearranged

parts.note: taken as written

explanation.surface: The goddess of love has gentle grooming skills and subtle artistry.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Venus' points to the goddess, but it is the planet; 'usually' is there because other planets can also be the evening star.
explanation.definitionFit: The evening star is the bright planet seen in the west after sunset, which is most often Venus.

clue.text: Large piece of land in eastern nation

parts.note: standard abbreviation
a state is a nation

explanation.surface: A huge landholding located in an Eastern country.
explanation.definitionFit: An estate is an extensive area of land owned by one person or family, usually with a large house.

clue.text: Oil extracted from greener olives

indicators.note: something extracted from words is drawn out of them, so the letters sit inside the run of text

parts.note: spans the end of the first word and the start of the second

explanation.surface: An oil pressed out of unripe olives.
explanation.walkthrough: The surface suggests olive oil, but the answer is a different oil entirely, from orange blossom.
explanation.definitionFit: Neroli is an essential oil distilled from the flowers of the bitter orange, used in perfume.
